jane (support): FYI - customer ACME reported a big invoice delta. Invoice INV-3342 shows ~1.2M billed tokens for Feb 3-4 but their dashboard 'served tokens' shows ~600k. Can someone take a look?

alex (eng): Got it. Can you paste a couple sample request_ids + timeframe and which model/route they were using?

jane (support): Sample IDs: rq_8f3a2, rq_8f3a8, timeframe 2025-02-03 02:00 -> 2025-02-04 14:00 UTC. Using /v1/generate with model=redwood-2-large and continuous-batcher=v2 enabled on their Dedicated pool. Invoice PDF: https://invoices.internal/INV-3342 (internal link).

sam (eng-ml): Quick thought — continuous prefetch / prefix KV warmups can generate internal requests that the runtime processes. Metering should exclude warmup-only traffic, but I have seen edge cases where the batching path counts tokens before the response is suppressed to the client.

maria (billing): To be clear: our billing pipeline normally counts tokens at the meter emission point which should be tied to response emission. Do we have evidence tokens were emitted to meter separate from served responses?

alex (eng): I pulled logs for rq_8f3a2. Short excerpt: 
```
[2025-02-03T03:12:10Z] batcher: enqueuing req rq_8f3a2
[2025-02-03T03:12:10Z] batcher: prefetch warmup req warmup-req-175
[2025-02-03T03:12:10Z] runtime: executed 820 tokens for warmup-req-175
[2025-02-03T03:12:10Z] meter: emitted billed_tokens=820 request_id=warmup-req-175
[2025-02-03T03:12:11Z] runtime: served client tokens=60 request_id=rq_8f3a2
[2025-02-03T03:12:11Z] meter: emitted billed_tokens=60 request_id=rq_8f3a2
```
Looks like the warmup request generated a meter emission. Warmup-req is internal and not associated with the customer dashboard, but currently our meterer tagged it to the pool owner causing a billed charge.

jane (support): OK that matches the pattern the customer mentioned — billed > served. Can you reproduce locally so we can explain to them and propose a credit?

sam (eng-ml): Repro steps I used (minimal):
1) start a small Dedicated pool with continuous-batcher enabled and prefix-cache on
2) send 200 short requests in rapid succession with the same prompt prefix
3) watch runtime logs for warmup-prefetch entries and meter emissions
Example curl: 
```
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"prompt":"translate: hello","max_tokens":64}' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate &\
done
```
You should see internal warmup requests run and billed token emissions that are not visible in the dashboard served-token counter (dashboard ties to client response IDs).

alex (eng): Short-term mitigation: disable continuous prefetch for the customer's pool (config flag: `continuous_prefetch:false`) or temporarily set batching window smaller so warmups don't run as often. Longer term we should change metering to only attribute meter emissions that are tagged as "served" or have an exported response_id linked to a client request.

maria (billing): We'll prepare a provisional credit for the delta while eng provides a repro + root cause. Please include exact billed token ids and meter events so finance can match.

jane (support): I'll tell the customer we have a suspected warmup accounting bug and we'll propose a credit + short-term disable. They asked how permanent the fix is — timeline?

eng-oncall-bot (eng-oncall-bot): Created internal ticket: INFRA-1229 "metering: exclude internal warmup/prefetch from billed tokens" assigned to eng-ml.

sam (eng-ml): ETA: patch in two weeks to make the meterer check for `internal_warmup=true` tag and not bill those emissions. I'll post a repro script and the log-parsing snippet tomorrow.

alex (eng): Follow-ups: 1) maria - list invoice IDs for credit; 2) sam - add tests in continuous-batcher integration tests; 3) jane - reply to customer with the short-term disable and that we will credit verified delta. :thumbsup:

maria (billing): Confirmed invoice list requested. Will hold any collections on INV-3342 until we finalize.

jane (support): Thanks all — I'll send a customer note and attach the ticket.

sam (eng-ml): P.S. repro corner case: if the KV cache prefix returns a cold miss, the prefetch does a full forward which can be hundreds of tokens. That's the main source of the large deltas. Keep an eye on clients with high prefix-repeat traffic.
